message:
Blog post slugs now keep the base letter of accented characters: "Crème brûlée recipes" becomes `creme-brulee-recipes`. `npm test` passes all 3 tests, including `test/blog-slug.test.js`.

**Cause:** `src/blog/slug.js` calls the vendored `slugify`, which is pinned at 1.2.0. Its changelog says 1.2.1 added transliteration of accented letters, so the old version strips them.

**Fix:** In `src/blog/slug.js`, `postSlug` now decomposes accents (NFD) and removes the combining marks before calling `slugify`. I did not touch `vendor/`, per CLAUDE.md. The fix is a one-line change plus a comment, and only `src/blog/slug.js` is modified.

**Not done:**
- The real fix is upgrading `vendor/slugify` to 1.2.1. That is the platform team's job, and once it lands my workaround is redundant and can be removed.
- `src/shop/product-url.js` also calls the same `slugify`, so product URLs will still drop accents (e.g. "Crème brûlée" → `crme-brle`). I left it alone because the task was about blog posts. Say the word if you want the same fix there.

I did not commit anything.
